What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0178-0113 showed the wellhead at 11.2 °C with the air at 8.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0178-033

Asset: WELL-0178 (NE-08 Well 178, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 28 Jun 2026 08:00 · Finished: 01 Jul 2026 15:00 · Well stopped for this job: 79 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0178-0187 on 2026-06-25 Report written: 02 Jul 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0178-0187 showed the wellhead at 43.5 °C with the air at 38.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 1 day longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 242 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 194 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0178-033 (WS-06).
